o: Define a[i] = nums1[i] - nums2[i]. The condition nums1[i] - nums1[j] <= nums2[i] - nums2[j] + diff rearranges to a[i] - a[j] <= diff, i.e., a[j] >= a[i] - diff. So we must count pairs i < j with a[j] at least a[i] - diff — a classic 'count inverted-ish pairs' problem. In example 1, a = [1,0,4] and all three pairs qualify. n up to 1e5 rules out O(n²); we need divide-and-conquer (merge sort) or a Fenwick tree over compressed values.
k: Subtract the arrays first: count pairs i<j with a[j] >= a[i] - diff.
Both merge sort and a BIT solve this in O(n log n); answers fit in 64-bit (up to ~5e9 pairs).

a.i: During merge sort, when both halves are sorted, for each i in the left half advance a pointer j into the right half to the first position with a[j] >= a[i] - diff; all elements from j onward form valid pairs. Summing these counts before merging yields the answer.
s: Transform to array a = nums1 - nums2.
Recursively sort halves; before merging, two-pointer count pairs across halves.
a.t: O(n log n) — standard merge sort with O(n) cross counting per level

a.n: Approach 2: Fenwick tree over compressed values
a.i: Sweep i from left to right. Before inserting a[i], query how many previously inserted values are >= a[i] - diff; that is exactly the number of valid j < i for this i. Coordinate-compress the values since they fit in [-3e4, 3e4].
s: Compress all values a[i] and thresholds a[i]-diff into ranks.
For each i ascending: answer += (number inserted) - (count of inserted values < a[i]-diff).
Insert rank of a[i] into the BIT.

c.python:
import bisect
class Solution:
    def numberOfPairs(self, nums1: List[int], nums2: List[int], diff: int) -> int:
        a = [x - y for x, y in zip(nums1, nums2)]
        sv = sorted(set(a))
        m = len(sv)
        tree = [0] * (m + 1)
        def upd(i):
            i += 1
            while i <= m:
                tree[i] += 1
                i += i & -i
        def qry(i):
            s = 0
            while i > 0:
                s += tree[i]
                i -= i & -i
            return s
        ans = 0
        for i, x in enumerate(a):
            lo = bisect.bisect_left(sv, x - diff)
            ans += i - qry(lo)
            upd(bisect.bisect_left(sv, x))
        return ans

a.t: O(n log n) — compression sort plus n BIT operations of O(log n)

w: The transformation to a[i] = nums1[i]-nums2[i] is the crux; after that it is the standard 'count pairs with a[j] >= a[i] - diff' template. Use merge sort if you dislike BIT bookkeeping, BIT if you want an online sweep. Common pitfalls: integer overflow (answer up to ~n²/2 ≈ 5e9, use 64-bit) and forgetting to insert a[i] only after querying (to enforce i < j).
